public_body: Mbta Fiscal And Management Control Board
overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation in the December 5 litigation-strategy executive session or in the Board's failure to name the litigation, but recommended amending the inadequate executive session minutes.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board entered executive session on December 5 for an improper purpose (litigation strategy under Purpose 3).
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law by meeting in executive session on December 5 to discuss litigation strategy.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board failed to identify the litigation matter it intended to discuss before entering executive session.
allegations.key_passage: Looking at all that transpired prior to December 5, it was reasonable for Attorney Englander to anticipate litigation in response to the Board awarding a second contract to CRRC for additional rail cars rather than go through a competitive procurement process, and to advise the Board of the potential litigation consequences of this decision.

allegations.summary: Not raised by the complaint; the AG reviewed the December 5 executive session minutes in camera and found them insufficiently detailed.
allegations.key_passage: we note that the minutes are inadequate to meet the standard required by the Open Meeting Law because they do not offer a sufficiently detailed summary of the Board's ninety minute discussions.

remedy: Amend the December 5 executive session minutes to meet the detail requirements of G.L. c. 30A, § 22(a) (recommendation).
Withhold minutes only while disclosure would defeat the executive session's purpose; then publicly release them (conditional, per G.L. c. 30A, § 22(f)).
remedy_passage: We recommend that the Board amend its December 5 executive session meeting minutes in accordance with the requirements of G.L. c. 30A, § 22(a).
